name: Muji Yi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Pelkey, Jamin (2011). Dialectology as Dialectic: Interpreting Phula Variation. Berlin: De Gruyter (covers Muji varieties incl. phonological sketches); retired ISO code split into ymc/ymi/ymq/ymx/ymz in 2008

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. A Phula Comparative Lexicon: Phola, Phuza, Muji, Phowa, Azha. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 18. Dallas: SIL International. 144 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. Sec. 3.3 'Southern Muji phonology in brief' pp. 8-9: {(C)(V)VT} template, segment table, 'five pitch contrasts' 55/33/13/21/52, sandhi ([22-21], [22-21-21]), tense voice non-contrastive but co-articulated with /21/ and /13/, nasalization non-contrastive; sec. 4.6 Muji meso-clade pp. 15-16 = subgrouping/tone history. The words stress/accent do not occur in the book; 'sesquisyllabic' (p. 11-12) concerns Azha rhotacized onsets, not Muji.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority / Pelkey, Jamin R. 2007. Change Request 2007-120: split [ymj] Muji Yi into [ymc] Southern Muji, [ymx] Northern Muji, [ymq] Qila Muji, [ymi] Moji, [ymz] Muzi (adopted 2008-01-14); plus Request for New Language Code Element [ymc] Muji, Southern. SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; identity, intelligibility-test and location data only. States Southern Muji is 'the most vital and prototypical Muji variety' and that 'very little research has been carried out among them'; sole source cited is Pelkey 2008 PhD.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2007. Muji's mirrored merger: correlative redistribution of checked tone classes in a newly defined Burmic cluster. Mon-Khmer Studies 37: 179-195.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. Sec. 2 'Sample phonology sketch' (pp. 181-183) of Muji-PJZ (= Southern Muji): syllable C(V)VT, 34 initials, 9+9 vowels, 'five contrastive tones 55, 33, 13, 21, 52' with pitch plots, sandhi rules, phonation non-contrastive. No mention of stress, accent or syllable prominence anywhere in the article (full scanned read).

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2005. Puzzling over Phula: toward the synthesis and statement of a sub-branch. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 28(2): 43-78.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Muji phonology; literature survey shows Chinese local sources on Muji (HHYC 2003, MZXZ 1995, GJMZ 1990) give only classification remarks and lexical-similarity percentages: 'very little linguistic data is ever offered in these sources' (p. 56).

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. Dialectology as Dialectic: Interpreting Phula Variation. Trends in Linguistics. Studies and Monographs 229. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. xxxiv+498 pp. (ch. 5 'Phula phonologies: five representative sketches', pp. 223-270, incl. sec. 5.3 Muji-PJZ and the Muji clade; sec. 6.3 Muji meso-clade)

sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL3311.Y5 P45 2011
sources.note: The fullest published phonological sketch of Muji-PJZ and clade-wide Muji phonology by the only fieldworker; would supersede the two brief sketches read here. Google Books full-text index returns 0 hits for stress/stressed/unstressed/iambic/sesquisyllabic, so it is probably also silent, but only the full text can confirm.
